name: Die Cut Car Stickers
seoTitle: Die Cut Car Stickers and Bumper Stickers Cut to Shape
seoDescription: Die cut car stickers in laminated outdoor vinyl, cut to your artwork outline for bumpers, rear windows, doors and motorcycle fairings. Free proof.
tagline: Laminated outdoor vinyl cut to your logo shape, rated for car washes, sun and road salt.
quickAnswer: Die cut car stickers are printed on laminated outdoor vinyl and cut to the outline of the artwork for bumpers, rear glass, doors, tailgates and motorcycle fairings. They suit car clubs, small fleets, dealerships and anyone who wants a logo on a vehicle without a rectangle around it. Sizes run from 2 to 24 inches, pricing starts from $0.30 per sticker with a 100 piece minimum, and production takes 5 to 7 business days after proof approval.

sections.h2: Outline-cut shapes for bumpers, glass and body panels
sections.html:
A car is the hardest place a sticker will ever live. It bakes on a July afternoon, gets blasted at the car wash, picks up road salt in winter and sits in the rain for days. A die cut car sticker meets that with a laminated outdoor vinyl cut to the shape of the artwork, so there is no square of white around a round logo and no sharp corner for a brush to catch.

Our custom car stickers page is the sibling. It covers the standard formats: the 3 by 10 inch bumper rectangle, oval euro-style stickers, window rectangles and large door panels. That page suits a slogan or a phone number in a box. This one is for the shape itself: a team crest on a rear window, a mascot on a tailgate, a club logo on a fairing. When the message is text in a box rather than a shape, the custom car sticker page is the cheaper route because rectangles nest tighter on the sheet.

sections.h2: Placement guide: where the sticker goes and what it faces
sections.html:
Where on the vehicle you put a sticker changes what it has to survive and which build we recommend.

LocationSurfaceExposureRecommended build
Rear window, outsideGlassSun, wipers, washesLaminated white vinyl, 4 to 8 inches
Rear window, insideGlass, reverse appliedHeat behind glassClear vinyl, mirrored print, white ink
BumperPainted plasticGravel, salt, car wash brushesLaminated vinyl, gloss, rounded shapes
Door or tailgatePainted metalSun, washes, door dingsLaminated vinyl, 8 to 24 inches
Motorcycle tank or fairingCurved painted metal or plasticFuel, gloves, vibrationLaminated 3 mil vinyl, under 6 inches

Two placements to avoid: the top of the dashboard, where heat under the windshield cooks adhesive within a season, and any plastic trim with a textured grain, which the vinyl bridges rather than grips.

sections.h2: Why the laminate matters on a vehicle
sections.html:
Printed ink on bare vinyl survives on a laptop. On a car it fades and scuffs within a year or two, because the ink is the top surface and it takes every hit. A laminate is a clear vinyl film bonded over the print, and it changes what the sticker can take:

  • UV light hits the laminate first, so the color underneath keeps its depth for three to five years instead of one or two
  • Car wash brushes and drying towels scuff the film, not the ink
  • Gasoline drips, bug spray and bird droppings wipe off without lifting color
  • The extra thickness resists the edge curl that starts at a bumper corner
  • Matte laminate kills the glare on a rear window, gloss laminate keeps the color at its richest

Every car sticker on this page ships laminated. We also use the same construction on the other vehicle and outdoor pieces listed under our stickers by use category, so the choice is really gloss or matte rather than laminate or not.

sections.h2: Applying to a car so the sticker stays put
sections.html:
1. Wash the area, then wipe it with isopropyl alcohol to remove wax and detailing spray. Wax is the main reason car stickers lift early.
  2. Work in the shade with the panel between 50 and 90 degrees Fahrenheit. A hot panel grabs the vinyl before you can position it.
  3. Place the sticker with the backing on and mark the edges with masking tape.
  4. Peel the backing halfway, align the sticker, and press the exposed half down from the center outward with a credit card or squeegee.
  5. Peel the rest of the backing and squeegee the second half the same way, pushing air toward the edges.
  6. Press every edge again firmly with your thumb, especially on a bumper curve.
  7. Keep it dry for 24 hours and out of the car wash for 72 hours while the adhesive cures.

sections.h2: Removing and replacing a die cut car sticker
sections.html:
A permanent adhesive sticker on factory paint comes off cleanly with heat. Warm it with a hair dryer or a heat gun on low for 20 to 30 seconds, lift one edge with a plastic razor blade and pull at a low angle while keeping the heat on the vinyl. Residue wipes off with a citrus adhesive remover or isopropyl alcohol, then re-wax the spot. Never use a metal blade on paint or glass tint.

Expect a faint ghost on an older car, because the paint around the sticker has faded while the paint under it has not. That is sun damage to the paint, not the sticker. If you change designs each season, ask for the removable adhesive at ordering; it trades some car-wash resistance for an easy peel. Removal and surface prep work the same way for every sticker we print, and our main custom sticker page lists the adhesive options across the whole range.

sections.h2: Sizes and quantities for clubs, teams and small fleets
sections.html:
A rear window logo reads from the car behind at 5 to 8 inches wide. A bumper piece looks right at 4 to 6 inches. Door and tailgate graphics for a work truck run 12 to 24 inches and we can tile larger. Motorcycle and helmet pieces stay under 6 inches so they can wrap a curve without creasing.

The minimum is 100 stickers per design. Car clubs often split that across two or three sizes of the same crest, which we allow. Fleet buyers usually order a size per vehicle type and keep spares for replacements after bodywork. Production is 5 to 7 business days after proof approval and FedEx delivery is free within the United States, with everything arriving inside 8 to 10 business days.

faqs.q: Do die cut car stickers survive automatic car washes?
faqs.a: Yes, once the adhesive has cured for 72 hours. The laminate takes the brush contact and the drying blowers instead of the ink. Touchless washes are gentler still. The one habit to avoid is aiming a pressure washer wand at a sticker edge from a few inches away, which can start a lift.

faqs.q: Can a die cut bumper sticker be removed without damaging the paint?
faqs.a: Yes, on factory paint that is in good condition. Heat the sticker with a hair dryer, lift an edge with a plastic razor and peel slowly at a low angle. Clean the residue with citrus remover and re-wax. Resprayed or peeling clear coat is the exception; test a corner there first.

faqs.q: Which side of the window do die cut car stickers go on?
faqs.a: Outside, for a standard white vinyl sticker, because the adhesive faces the glass and the print faces out. If you want the sticker inside the glass, out of the weather, order a clear vinyl version printed in reverse with a white ink backer. Tinted film on the inside is a separate issue; stickers should not go on aftermarket tint.

faqs.q: How long will a die cut car sticker last in the sun?
faqs.a: Three to five years is typical for a laminated sticker on a door, bumper or outside glass. Dashboards and rear decks under glass run hotter and fade sooner. Gloss laminate holds color depth slightly longer than matte, and lighter colors show fading less than deep reds and blues.

faqs.q: Do die cut car stickers work on motorcycle tanks and helmets?
faqs.a: Yes, with two limits. Keep the piece under about 6 inches so it conforms to the curve without creasing, and avoid shapes with long thin tails that cannot bend. Fuel splashes wipe off the laminate without harm. On a helmet, apply only to the smooth shell, never over vents.

faqs.q: What size works for a die cut sticker on a rear window?
faqs.a: Between 5 and 8 inches wide reads from the next car at a stoplight. Go smaller and the logo becomes a shape nobody can identify; go wider than 10 inches and it starts to block the mirror view. Measure the flat area of your glass above the defroster lines before choosing.

faqs.q: Can die cut car stickers be printed in a Pantone fleet color?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the Pantone reference and we match it in CMYK on the proof, which you approve before the run. For a single flat color on a fleet of vans, a cut vinyl decal in a solid film is an even closer match, and we can quote both so you can compare.

faqs.q: Are die cut car stickers different from vinyl car decals?
faqs.a: Yes. A die cut car sticker is a printed, laminated piece on a backing that you peel and stick, best under 24 inches. A car decal is usually cut vinyl lettering or a large graphic applied with transfer tape. Decals suit fleet lettering and big panels; stickers suit logos, crests and shapes.

faqs.q: What temperature is best for applying die cut car stickers?
faqs.a: Between 50 and 90 degrees Fahrenheit, with the panel in the shade. Below 50 the adhesive stays stiff and does not bond fully; above 90, or on a sun-heated panel, the vinyl grabs instantly and you lose the chance to reposition. In Phoenix that means early morning in summer.

faqs.q: Can I order 100 die cut car stickers for a car club?
faqs.a: Yes, 100 per design is the minimum, and you can split it across sizes of the same crest, for example 50 at 4 inches for bumpers and 50 at 7 inches for rear windows. Pricing starts from $0.30 per sticker and depends on size, so the mix affects the total; a quote spells it out.

faqs.q: Will gas, road salt or bugs damage a die cut car sticker?
faqs.a: Not the laminated ones. Gasoline that drips at the filler wipes off the laminate without lifting ink, road salt rinses away at the car wash, and bug residue comes off with a damp cloth if it is not left to bake for weeks. Unlaminated stickers would stain in all three cases, which is why we laminate every car piece.

faqs.q: How fast can die cut car stickers be printed for an event?
faqs.a: Standard production is 5 to 7 business days after proof approval, and free FedEx delivery brings the total to 8 to 10 business days anywhere in the United States. For a car show or a dealer launch with a fixed date, tell us the date on the quote request and we will confirm whether a rush run fits.
